info.title: API Reference
info.description: Custom document-processing APIs powered by PDF Vector

post.summary: Ask a question about a document
post.description: Parse a document and answer a question about its content using AI. Supports PDF, Word (.docx), Excel (.xlsx), PowerPoint (.pptx), CSV, Image (.png, .jpg, .tiff, .bmp, .heif), Plain Text (.txt, .md, .tsv, .xml), RTF, HTML, OpenDocument (.odt, .ods, .odp), EPUB, and Bibliography (.bib, .ris, .nbib, .enw) files. Files up to 1000 pages and up to 500MB in size. Provide the document via file upload, a public URL, or a base64-encoded string.

url.description: URL of the document file to fetch and parse

file.description: Document file upload via multipart form-data (PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, CSV, PNG, JPG, TIFF, BMP, HEIF, TXT, MD, TSV, XML, RTF, HTML, ODT, ODS, ODP, EPUB, BIB, RIS, NBIB, ENW)

question.description: The question to answer about the document

model.description:
Model tier for answering the question.

- auto (default): Automatically selects the best tier — credits based on the tier selected.
- nano: 2 credits/page. Fastest. Best for simple questions about straightforward documents.
- mini: 4 credits/page. Balanced speed and accuracy. Moderately complex questions.
- pro: 8 credits/page. High accuracy for nuanced questions about complex documents.
- max: 16 credits/page. Maximum accuracy. Best for difficult questions requiring deep reasoning.

Supported formats by tier:
- All tiers: PDF, Word (.docx), Excel (.xlsx), PowerPoint (.pptx), CSV, Text (.txt, .md, .tsv, .xml), HTML, RTF, OpenDocument (.odt, .ods, .odp), EPUB, Bibliography (.bib, .ris, .nbib, .enw).
- Pro/Max/Auto adds: Image (PNG, JPG, TIFF, BMP, HEIF). Image dimensions must be between 50×50 and 10000×10000 pixels.

documentId.description: Optional external document ID for usage attribution. The x-pdfvector-document-id header takes precedence when both are provided.

url.description: Webhook URL where results will be POSTed when processing completes

callback.description: Optional webhook callback for async processing. When provided, the server returns 202 immediately and POSTs the full response payload to the callback URL when processing completes. On error, the callback receives a POST with X-Pdfvector-Callback-Failed: true header and error details in the body. Useful for long-running operations that may exceed client timeout limits.
